title: NO ONE MAY SEE MY FACE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'But,' he said, 'you cannot see my face, for no one may see me and live.'" - Exod 33:20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
There is a limit, and God states it plainly. Not because He is stingy, but because we are small and He is holy. Unshielded divine glory would not enrich a sinner; it would end him.

We live in a time that resists limits, including spiritual ones. We want full understanding, complete explanations, God fully mapped. But some of God's "no" answers are protective. A God we could fully comprehend would be a God small enough to be no God at all.

Isaiah saw a vision of the Lord and cried "Woe to me! I am ruined!" (Isa 6:5). That is the honest human response to holiness.

So how does this end? Not in permanent distance. John writes that no one has ever seen God, but the one and only Son has made Him known (John 1:18). In Christ, the glory that would have destroyed us was veiled in flesh so that we could look and live.

And there is more coming. One day we shall see Him as He is (1 John 3:2), and His servants will see His face (Rev 22:4) — because we will finally be made fit for it.

What Moses could not have, we are promised.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you at peace with not understanding everything about God?
2. How does God's holiness shape the way you approach Him?
3. What does it mean to you that one day you will see His face?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy God, I cannot bear Your unveiled glory, yet in Christ I may come near. Thank You for the day when I shall see You. Amen.
